@@ -0,0 +1,9 @@
+---
+"@sitoo/iam-mono-iam-api": minor
+---
+
+Add explicit sign-in permissions `backoffice.login` (client `bo`) and `pos.login` (client `pos`) to the permission catalog.
+
+System roles now grant sign-in for every client they already use: roles holding Backoffice permissions get `backoffice.login`, roles holding POS permissions get `pos.login`. `sitoo-store-staff` stays POS-only and `sitoo-viewer` stays Backoffice-only.
+
+Migration `007_add_login_permissions` backfills existing custom roles by the same rule — any role with at least one granted `bo` permission gets `bo:backoffice.login`, any role with at least one granted `pos` permission gets `pos:pos.login`. System roles are skipped (they resolve permissions from the code catalog), as are soft-deleted roles. The migration is idempotent.

@@ -39,6 +39,13 @@ Role {
 
 ## Permission catalog (permissions + actions)
 
+### Sign-in
+
+- `backoffice`: login — required to sign in to Backoffice (client `bo`)
+- `pos`: login — required to sign in to POS (client `pos`)
+
+Sign-in is an explicit permission: without `backoffice.login` a user cannot reach Backoffice at all, and without `pos.login` cannot reach POS, no matter which other permissions the role grants. Every standard role holding any Backoffice permission also holds `backoffice.login`, and every one holding any POS permission also holds `pos.login` — so `sitoo-store-staff` (POS-only) has no `backoffice.login`, and `sitoo-viewer` (Backoffice-only) has no `pos.login`. Migration `007_add_login_permissions` backfills both keys onto pre-existing custom roles by the same rule.
+
 ### Omni Flows
 
 - `orders`: read, write

@@ -0,0 +1,60 @@
+-- Backfill the new sign-in permissions onto existing roles:
+--   bo:backoffice.login  -> every role already holding any bo permission
+--   pos:pos.login        -> every role already holding any pos permission
+-- Rationale: sign-in is now an explicit permission, so roles that could use a
+-- client before this release must keep being able to sign in to that client.
+--
+-- Only non-system roles are touched. System roles resolve their permissions
+-- from the code catalog at runtime (see system-roles.catalog.ts), which grants
+-- both keys directly, so rows written for them here would only be redundant
+-- overrides. Soft-deleted roles are skipped.
+--
+-- "Holding a permission" means an explicit grant — a role whose only rows for a
+-- client are `deny` overrides is not treated as a user of that client.
+--
+-- Idempotent: ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING against uq_role_perm
+-- (role_id, client, permission_key).
+
+INSERT INTO role_permissions (
+    id, role_id, client, permission_key, modifier, created_at
+)
+SELECT
+    gen_random_uuid(),
+    r.id,
+    'bo',
+    'backoffice.login',
+    'grant',
+    NOW()
+FROM roles r
+WHERE r.is_system = false
+  AND r.deleted_at IS NULL
+  AND EXISTS (
+      SELECT 1
+      FROM role_permissions rp
+      WHERE rp.role_id = r.id
+        AND rp.client = 'bo'
+        AND rp.modifier = 'grant'
+  )
+ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;
+
+INSERT INTO role_permissions (
+    id, role_id, client, permission_key, modifier, created_at
+)
+SELECT
+    gen_random_uuid(),
+    r.id,
+    'pos',
+    'pos.login',
+    'grant',
+    NOW()
+FROM roles r
+WHERE r.is_system = false
+  AND r.deleted_at IS NULL
+  AND EXISTS (
+      SELECT 1
+      FROM role_permissions rp
+      WHERE rp.role_id = r.id
+        AND rp.client = 'pos'
+        AND rp.modifier = 'grant'
+  )
+ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;
